source_text:
Οὐκέτι θέλω κατὰ ἀνθρώπους ζῆν. τοῦτο δὲ ἔσται, ἐὰν ὑμεῖς θελήσητε. θελήσατε, ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς θεληθῆτε.
δἰ ὀλίγων γραμμάτων αἰτοῦμαι ὑμᾶς: πιστεύσατέ μοι. Ἰησοῦς δὲ Χριστὸς ὑμῖν ταῦτα φανερώσει, ὅτι ἀληθῶς λέγω: τὸ ἀψευδὲς στόμα, ἐν ᾧ ὁ πατὴρ ἐλάλησεν ἀληθῶς.
αἰτήσασθε περὶ ἐμοῦ, ἵνα ἐπιτύχω. οὐ κατὰ σάρκα ὑμῖν ἔγραψα, ἀλλὰ κατὰ γνώμην θεοῦ. ἐὰν πάθω, ἠθελήσατε: ἐὰν ἀποδοκιμασθῶ, ἐμισήσατε.
thought_title: No longer living according to men
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Romans, telling them he no longer wants to live in a merely human way and asking them to pray that he may attain God.
pass_a_gloss: No longer do I want to live according to men. This will happen, if you wish it. Wish it, so that you also may be wished for. Through a few letters I ask you: believe me. Jesus Christ will reveal these things to you, that I speak truly: the mouth that does not lie, in which the Father spoke truly. Ask concerning me, so that I may attain. Not according to flesh did I write to you, but according to the mind of God. If I suffer, you wished it: if I am rejected, you hated me.

choices.why: Keeps the prepositional force of κατὰ with the plural ἀνθρώπους, meaning a merely human standard of life, not 'as a man'
rejected: to live in a human way

choices.english: Wish it, so that you also may be wished for
choices.why: Preserves the passive of θέλω and the reciprocity of the wish; the Romans' willing enables their being willed by God
rejected: Desire it, that you also may be desired
Will it, that you also may be willed

choices.english: the mouth that does not lie
choices.why: Renders the alpha-privative adjective as a relative clause to keep the noun phrase natural in English while retaining the negation

choices.english: according to the mind of God
choices.why: γνώμη here means God's settled purpose or will, and 'mind' preserves the noun's deliberative sense
rejected: according to the will of God

choices.why: ἀποδοκιμάζω means to reject after testing, and the passive keeps the judicial force of being found unworthy

pass_b_english: I no longer want to live by human standards. And this will happen if you wish it. Wish it, so that you too may be wished for.

Through these few lines I ask you: believe me. And Jesus Christ will reveal these things to you, showing that I speak truly. He is the mouth that does not lie, through which the Father has truly spoken.

Ask on my behalf, so that I may attain it. I have written to you not according to the flesh, but according to the mind of God. If I suffer, it will be because you wished it. If I am rejected, it will be because you hated me.

problems.quote: if I am rejected, you hated me.
problems.why: Greek says ‘you have condemned/rejected me’, not ‘you hated me’. The nuance of judgment is lost.
problems.fix: If I am rejected, you have condemned me.

edits.old: If I suffer, you wished it; if I am rejected, you hated me.
edits.new: If I suffer, you wished it; if I am rejected, you have condemned me.

problems.quote: If I suffer, you wished it; if I am rejected, you have condemned me.
problems.source_quote: ἐὰν πάθω, ἠθελήσατε: ἐὰν ἀποδοκιμασθῶ, ἐμισήσατε.
problems.why: Source says 'you desired/willed it' and 'you hated me'; English 'condemned' mistranslates ἐμισήσατε (hated).
problems.fix: If I suffer, you desired it; if I am rejected, you hated me.
problems.ruling: Greek ἐμισήσατε = 'you hated', not 'condemned'; English misrepresents the verb's meaning.

edits.old: If I suffer, you wished it; if I am rejected, you have condemned me.
edits.new: If I suffer, you desired it; if I am rejected, you hated me.

fixed: Changed 'you have condemned me' to 'you hated me' to match the source verb ἐμισήσατε, and 'you wished it' to 'you desired it' to match ἠθελήσατε.

problems.quote: Wish it, so that you also may be wished for
problems.why: Circular and nonsensical as English; probably means 'wish for my death, so that you may be wished for [by God]'.
problems.fix: 'Wish it, so that you too may be found worthy.'

edits.old: Wish it, so that you also may be wished for.
edits.new: Wish it, so that you too may be wished for.

fixed: The English 'Wish it, so that you also may be wished for' accurately renders the source 'θελήσατε, ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς θεληθῆτε' (wish it, so that you also may be wished for). The suggested fix 'found worthy' is not in the source. I made only a minor stylistic adjustment from 'you also' to 'you too' for naturalness, which does not change the meaning.

polish.changed: Clarified the final conditional as future consequence, identified Jesus Christ as the truthful mouth, and smoothed sentence flow for reading aloud.

notes.quote: If I suffer, you desired it; if I am rejected, you hated me
notes.why: Paradoxical and seemingly accusatory; reader cannot tell if this is conditional or a statement of fact.
notes.fix: Add note: Ignatius means 'if I suffer, it will show that you desired my martyrdom; if I am rejected [from martyrdom], it will show you hated [the idea]'.
